name: Question 2
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=-7{x}^{2}+4$ defined on $[-3,3).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension of $G(x)=-14x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
-7{x}^{2}+4∼-17+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{252(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}}
and
{{field-3}}
on $R,$ we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
-14x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-4}}\cdot {{field-5}}.
$$

Question 2

Let f(x) be the 6-periodic extension of the function F(x)=−7x2+4 defined on [−3,3). Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the 6-periodic extension of G(x)=−14x from the corresponding Fourier series of f(x).The Fourier series of f(x) is given by
cos⁡(nπx3)
cos⁡(nπx6)
cos⁡(nπx3)
sin⁡(nπx6)
sin⁡(nπx3)
−7x2+4∼−17+∑n=1∞252(−1)n+1n2π2{(cos⁡(nπx6))(S0)}.

Since f is
 
odd
continuous
even
and
 
piecewise smooth
periodic
piecewise linear
on R, we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get
 
84(−1)n+1nπ
84(−1)nnπ
252(−1)nn2π2
252(−1)n+1n2π2
 
cos⁡(nπx3)
sin⁡(nπx3)
−14x∼∑n=1∞{(252(−1)n+1n2π2)(S3)}⋅{(cos⁡(nπx3))(S4)}.
